findings.summary: The fixed palette does not respond to the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The desktop and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are pixel-identical (both 302,124-byte captures before artifact normalization), and the DOM CSS uses fixed rgb(30,115,190) surfaces without a color-scheme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS/DOM probe found no view-transition rule, while the site exposes many route and listing-to-detail state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document or cross-document View Transitions, with a reduced-motion path, for listing-to-detail and menu state changes.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome remains static during a very long listing.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 12,484 CSS pixels tall on mobile, but DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state container query or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state-aware compact header or progress/position affordance on long lists.

findings.summary: The Actors dropdown relies on legacy scripted positioning rather than resilient anchor positioning.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS shows Bootstrap/Popper scripts in the head and no anchor-name/position-anchor/position-try rules for the navigation dropdown.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for the dropdown, retaining a simple fallback for older browsers.

findings.summary: Navigation changes provide little orientation or attention guidance.
findings.evidence: Screenshots show a dense filter/listing UI without breadcrumbs, current-location emphasis in the main navigation, scroll markers, or directional route transitions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear current-location state and directional transition/highlight cues when moving between listings and details.

findings.summary: A pop-under advertising script can interrupt ordinary interaction.
findings.evidence: HAR records a.pemsrv.com/popunder1000.js; an attempted mobile-menu click during the repeated-interaction test caused the inspected target to navigate or close.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove click-triggered pop-under behavior and keep ads inline, clearly labelled, bounded, and non-intercepting.

findings.summary: Transient navigation/advertising UI is built from legacy scripted elements rather than semantic primitives.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero dialog, popover, and details elements while the page has dropdown navigation and third-party ad frames driven by Bootstrap/Popper.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native popover/details/dialog primitives for transient and disclosure UI, with declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: Advertising and side chrome compete strongly with the primary content.
findings.evidence: Homepage and detail screenshots show 300×250 adult ads occupying large first-viewport regions; on detail the ad column competes directly with the player.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce above-the-fold ad density and reserve the dominant visual area for the requested listing or player.

findings.summary: Reusable components adapt only through viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rule; the actors template uses max-width media queries despite cards being reusable in multiple column contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/grid components containment and size-aware @container rules, with viewport rules only for page-level layout.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly exposed on primary links.
findings.evidence: The focus probe focused navigation and content links and computed outline-style none with no box shadow; several nav targets are only 40px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and raise interactive target dimensions to at least 44×44 CSS pixels where practical.

findings.summary: Advertising code can derail interaction before the user completes the browse/watch flow.
findings.evidence: A real click attempt on the mobile navigation caused CDP to report “Inspected target navigated or closed”; the HAR identifies popunder1000.js and multiple ad-network frames.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove global click interception/pop-under behavior and verify listing, search, navigation, and play flows end-to-end without unsolicited windows.

findings.summary: The 404 state is a dead end.
findings.evidence: The 404 screenshot and probe show only “Sorry, the page you visited does not exist” with no home, search, retry, or back link.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the site shell on 404s and offer Home, Search, and Back recovery actions.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP misses the good Core Web Vitals threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 2.9s and FCP 2.6s; the trace corroborated LCP/FCP around 1.95s under a lighter desktop run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP asset, shorten document latency, and defer non-critical ads/scripts until after primary content.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking dependencies and third-party delivery delay primary content.
findings.evidence: HAR flags four VeryHigh-priority stylesheets and non-deferred jQuery, Popper, and Bootstrap scripts in the head; live DOM confirms async=false/defer=false/type="".
findings.suggestedFix: Inline critical CSS selectively, defer non-critical CSS, and defer/remove head scripts not required for first render.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 90 KiB unused JS, including 70.8 KiB from Google Tag Manager and 21.8 KiB from jQuery; HAR records 252 KiB script transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused libraries and load analytics/advertising conditionally after consent or meaningful interaction.

findings.summary: Advertising frames lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: axe reports serious frame-title violations for the main ad iframe and injected 300×250 frames; DOM inspection confirms empty title values.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful frames a concise title, or mark purely decorative frames presentation/hidden from assistive technology.

findings.summary: Important safety copy fails WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: axe and Lighthouse both report 3.5:1 contrast for “Underage is strickly BANNED…” against #1e73be, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a lighter foreground or darker surface token that reaches at least 4.5:1 for normal text.

findings.summary: Landmark/list semantics and focus visibility are broken.
findings.evidence: axe reports nested complementary landmarks, invalid ul children, and content outside landmarks; the focus probe found no visible outline on tested links.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce a main landmark, repair list children and landmark nesting, and implement persistent :focus-visible styling in DOM order.

findings.summary: Media alternatives and some target sizes are insufficient.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found no track elements for video content, and tested navigation links measured 40px high; mobile reflow itself had zero horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide captions/transcripts for meaningful video and enlarge sub-44px controls without disabling zoom.

findings.summary: Images are delivered without robust intrinsic/responsive metadata.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 39/41 images missing dimensions, 38 missing srcset, and 39 oversized; Lighthouse also reports unsized image markup.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio and responsive srcset/sizes for each thumbnail and icon.

findings.summary: The platform stack includes blocked and legacy third-party behavior.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded Bootstrap 4.6.2 blocked by ORB, while DOM confirms legacy jQuery/Bootstrap/Popper head scripts and a click-triggered pop-under; Lighthouse best-practices scored 0.69.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the blocked dependency, migrate away from unnecessary legacy libraries, and eliminate global click interception.

findings.summary: Pages omit meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found no meta description on home or the representative detail; Lighthouse meta-description audit scored 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Write unique, accurate meta descriptions for the homepage and each public template.

findings.summary: robots.txt is blocked to a non-browser crawler.
findings.evidence: A direct robots.txt request returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 and a noindex block page, while sitemap.xml redirected successfully to wp-sitemap.xml.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow legitimate crawler access to robots.txt and keep robots, canonical, and sitemap policies consistent.

findings.summary: Rich content lacks accurate share metadata and uses questionable entity typing.
findings.evidence: Home has zero JSON-LD/OG tags; detail has no OG tags and wraps a VideoObject inside a MusicGroup despite being a video page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject/WebSite schema and Open Graph/Twitter metadata that matches visible content.

findings.summary: The document lacks baseline security headers and sets insecure analytics cookies.
findings.evidence: Headers found no CSP, HSTS, or nosniff; both _ga cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None for 400 days. HTTPS itself is present and no secrets were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff, and Secure/Lax analytics cookies with a shorter retention period.

findings.summary: Nearly the entire load is third-party and tracking starts by default.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 69/72 requests and 876,253/897,563 transferred bytes to third parties; tracker scan finds Google Tag Manager/Analytics among 15 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors, load optional analytics/ads only after clear consent, batch events, and document retention/purpose.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers reports no CSP/frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP with frame-ancestors, HSTS, nosniff, strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Third-party click handling makes runtime navigation fragile.
findings.evidence: The mobile-menu interaction caused the inspected target to navigate or close, and the network shows multiple ad frames plus popunder1000.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Isolate third-party ads in sandboxed frames and ensure site controls cannot be intercepted or close/navigate the active page.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling offers no useful recovery.
findings.evidence: The tested nonexistent route returns a branded-but-isolated 404 page with no links or site navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a lightweight site-shell 404 with search, home, and retry/back actions; add equivalent network/timeout messaging for dynamic surfaces.

findings.summary: The layout is not prepared for alternate writing directions.
findings.evidence: html lang is en-US, but the captured CSS relies on physical left/right/top/bottom positioning and no dir attribute is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain correct lang and migrate layout spacing/positioning to logical inline/block properties with RTL testing.

findings.summary: Rendered dates and durations appear single-locale and hand-formatted.
findings.evidence: Listing cards render fixed English relative strings such as “2 days ago” and pipe-separated duration/resolution text; no locale switch or localized formatting evidence was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Format dates, numbers, and durations with Intl APIs using the active locale.

findings.summary: Ordinary clicks can trigger unsolicited pop-under navigation.
findings.evidence: The loaded popunder1000.js coincides with a menu-click test closing/navigating the inspected target, which removes user control and disguises the commercial action.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove pop-under interception; make every commercial link explicit, labelled, and activated only by its own control.

findings.summary: Search explicitly disables browser input assistance.
findings.evidence: The only search input has autocomplete="off" and no accessible label was returned by the DOM form probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep search history/autocomplete available unless there is a documented privacy reason, and provide an explicit label.

findings.summary: Thumbnail delivery is not resolution or format efficient.
findings.evidence: Images audit found 40/41 legacy-format images, 38 without srcset, 39 oversized, and 34 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, srcset/sizes, intrinsic dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold thumbnails.

findings.summary: The homepage performs disproportionate eager background/network work.
findings.evidence: HAR records 72 requests including a 171,453-byte search JSON fetch and 69 third-party requests; DOM instantiates 38 video elements on the listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Fetch search/index data on demand, avoid pre-instantiating media, and deprioritize non-visible/background work.

findings.summary: Third-party ads, analytics, fonts, and scripts dominate the page budget.
findings.evidence: Third-party transfer is 876 KiB of 898 KiB total; above-the-fold screenshots show large ads, and 15 third-party origins are contacted.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove low-value vendors, defer ads below primary content, and self-host/subset essential fonts.
